title: Finite coefficient open restriction and normalized ordinary unit
statement: Let $j:U\hookrightarrow T$ be an open immersion of schemes and $A$ a finite, possibly noncommutative ring. The published continuous-function coefficient sheaves and transported module pullback [def-weil-pbc-proetale-modules, prop-weil-pbc-proetale-constant-exact] admit the natural coefficient-linear identification with evaluation over $T$, preserving constant scalars, restrictions, and module maps. The specified sectionwise pushforward is additive and right adjoint to this pullback. The unit is the actual small-model Kan unit and, under the evaluation identification, equals restriction along $V\times_T U\to V$ [def-weil-proetale-inverse-image, lem-pur-proetale-open-unit-evaluation].

proof.text: Let G be composition with the open immersion and F be base change. The continuous and cocontinuous G commutes with ring-valued sheafification. Apply Mathlib pushforwardContinuousSheafificationCompatibility to the continuous-function ring presheaf [def-weil-pbc-proetale-modules]. Its unit compatibility gives the coefficient isomorphism d and the equality on constant scalars. Continuity and cocontinuity are the concrete overMap results underlying [lem-weil-proetale-weakly-etale-localization].

The direct-image ring map of [prop-weil-pbc-proetale-constant-ring-map] is defined by sheafifying the continuous-function pullback. Precompose with the sheafification unit and apply its naturality to show that the site counit equals this ring map followed by d. Naturality of d and the site triangle identity give the other ringed-site adjunction equation. Mathlib pushforwardPushforwardAdj then constructs restriction as a left adjoint to the specified module pushforward. This is a direct ring-valued calculation, without commuting factors.

Use the existing finiteModuleAdjunction and finiteModuleAdjunction_existsUnique in Sheaf.AlgebraicGeometry.ProEtaleFiniteModuleAdjunction, the normalized finite-ring module interface for [def-weil-proetale-inverse-image]. Uniqueness of left adjoints identifies the actual transported pullback of [prop-weil-pbc-proetale-constant-exact] with the restriction functor. Take additive equivalences from its components; linearity and its two naturalities give all rho equations. The normalized-transpose theorem at the identity gives the model-unit equality. Mathlib unit_leftAdjointUniq_hom_app followed by pushforwardPushforwardAdj_unit_app_val_app gives restriction along the site counit, which is the specified first projection. Additivity is finiteModulePushforward_additive. Every step is proved in Lean.

theorem finiteCoefficientOpenRestriction {U T : Scheme.{u}} (j : U ⟶ T)
    [IsOpenImmersion j] (A : Type (u + 1))
    [Ring A] [Finite A] [TopologicalSpace A] [DiscreteTopology A] :
    ∃ d : (finiteCoefficientRingSheaf U A).obj ≅
        (Scheme.proEtaleOpenComposition j).op ⋙ (finiteCoefficientRingSheaf T A).obj,
      (∀ (W : U.ProEt) (a : A),
        (d.hom.app (op W)) ((finiteCoefficientScalarMap U A).app (op W) a) =
          (finiteCoefficientScalarMap T A).app
            (op ((Scheme.proEtaleOpenComposition j).obj W)) a) ∧
      ∃ rho : ∀ (N : FiniteCoefficientModules T A) (W : U.ProEt),
          ((finiteCoefficientModulePullback j A).obj N).val.obj (op W) ≃+
            N.val.obj (op ((Scheme.proEtaleOpenComposition j).obj W)),
        (∀ (N : FiniteCoefficientModules T A) (W : U.ProEt)
          (r : (finiteCoefficientRingSheaf U A).obj.obj (op W))
          (m : ((finiteCoefficientModulePullback j A).obj N).val.obj (op W)),
          rho N W (r • m) = (d.hom.app (op W) r) • rho N W m) ∧
        (∀ (N : FiniteCoefficientModules T A) (W W' : U.ProEt) (b : W' ⟶ W)
          (m : ((finiteCoefficientModulePullback j A).obj N).val.obj (op W)),
          rho N W' (((finiteCoefficientModulePullback j A).obj N).val.map b.op m) =
            N.val.map ((Scheme.proEtaleOpenComposition j).map b).op (rho N W m)) ∧
        (∀ (N N' : FiniteCoefficientModules T A) (h : N ⟶ N') (W : U.ProEt)
          (m : ((finiteCoefficientModulePullback j A).obj N).val.obj (op W)),
          rho N' W (((finiteCoefficientModulePullback j A).map h).val.app (op W) m) =
            h.val.app (op ((Scheme.proEtaleOpenComposition j).obj W)) (rho N W m)) ∧
        ∃ (_ : (SheafOfModules.pushforward.{u + 1} (F := Scheme.proEtaleBaseChange j)
            (J := Scheme.ProEt.topology T) (K := Scheme.ProEt.topology U)
            (finiteCoefficientDirectImageMap j A)).Additive)
          (adj : finiteCoefficientModulePullback j A ⊣ SheafOfModules.pushforward.{u + 1}
            (F := Scheme.proEtaleBaseChange j) (J := Scheme.ProEt.topology T)
            (K := Scheme.ProEt.topology U) (finiteCoefficientDirectImageMap j A)),
          (∀ (N : FiniteCoefficientModules T A) (V : T.ProEt) (m : N.val.obj (op V)),
            (adj.unit.app N).val.app (op V) m =
              (((SheafOfModules.pullbackPushforwardAdjunction.{u + 1}
                (finiteCoefficientModelRingUnit j A)).unit.app
                  ((Scheme.proEtaleModuleToModel (finiteCoefficientRingSheaf T A)).obj N)).val.app
                    (AsSmall.up.op.obj (op V))) m) ∧
          (∀ (N : FiniteCoefficientModules T A) (V : T.ProEt) (m : N.val.obj (op V)),
            rho N ((Scheme.proEtaleBaseChange j).obj V)
                ((adj.unit.app N).val.app (op V) m) =
              N.val.map (Scheme.proEtaleOpenSectionProjection j V).op m)
